summary: Kootenai NF site in Lincoln County: 1923 frame cab, 1940 pole tower with L-4 cab, now in ruins per NHLR and gone per FFLA; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: NHLR says the 1940 pole tower lies in ruins; firelookout.com repeats that wording; the FFLA Montana list marks the tower gone. No source supports a standing tower.
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

Vandalism and decay left the tower in ruins; no date given

corrections.why: The register attaches an L-4 cab to the 1940 pole tower. It mentions an L-6 cab about a mile northeast of the lookout as a separate structure, so L-6 does not describe the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Records had standing from firelookout.com and gone from FFLA. The firelookout.com page says the tower now lays in ruins, and the FFLA Montana list marks it gone; neither supports a standing tower. The FFLA list gives the NHLR number US 1504, MT 82 to a separate Elk Patrol row, which is a likely source of the standing reading.

notes_for_editor: NHLR and firelookout.com carry the same text, so they are effectively one account; the FFLA list is independent but terse. Do not confuse this tower with other Elk Mountain lookouts: a Sanders County Kootenai NF tower (firelookout.com elkmtn344, L-4 cab, 1935, destroyed 1955), a Flathead County tower (FFLA, 48.30673, -113.44420), a Missoula County site, a Glacier National Park tower in a Montana History Portal photo, and the Elk Mountain Trail in the Flathead NF near Whitefish, which is a different lookout. The FFLA list gives NHLR US 1504 to an 'Elk Patrol' row at 48.46258, -114.89668, which may be a mis-association. The record's height of 3.0 m is a rounding of the 10-foot tower (3.05 m). The L-6 cab's status is not stated anywhere. Access and visit facts are unknown and left out. No photo URLs found; the NHLR page has a photo section but no URL was read.
